Heard learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners and the learned counsel for respondents and perused the material on record.

3. In addition to reiterating the various contentions urged in the writ petition and referring to the material on record, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners submit that in the first instance,
during 2020-21, the respondents had passed awards in respect of lands other than the subject lands involved in the present petition.
However, subsequently, in respect of those lands, respondents passed second revised / modified awards reducing the quantum of compensation compared to the earlier awards.

The said second revised / modified awards were challenged by the land losers before this Court in the cases of Valerial Sequeria & Others Vs. SLAO & Competent Authority - W.P.No.10525/2021 & connected matters.

entities.text: Valerial Sequeria & Others Vs. SLAO & Competent Authority - W.P.No.10525/2021 &
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By final order dated 26.09.2022, the learned Single Judge of this Court set aside the second revised / modified awards and restored the first original awards which granted higher compensation and the said order passed by this Court has attained finality and become conclusive.

3.1 However, under the impugned awards passed in the present petitions, the respondents have awarded lesser / reduced compensation identical to the compensation awarded under the second revised / modified awards, though the same have been set aside by this Court in the aforesaid Sri Manohar Kudupu S/O Anantha Bhat vs Special Land Acquisition Officer And on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153029473/
5 decision

entities.text: Anantha Bhat vs Special Land Acquisition Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: as stated supra

. It si therefore contended that since the petitioners are identically and similarly situated to the other land losers who have been granted higher compensation as per the first / original awards, pursuant to the second revised / modified awards being quashed by this Court, the impugned awards, under which, the petitioners have been awarded compensation similar to that under the second revised / modified awards deserve to be set aside and higher compensation be awarded in favour of the petitioners as per the first / original awards passed by the respondents in respect of land losers relating to the same Notifications.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents submit that though the respondents have not challenged the order passed by this Court in Valerial Sequeria's case (supra), the earlier first /
original awards passed by them awarding higher compensation in favour of the land losers have been challenged by the respondents before the Deputy Commissioner/ Statutory Arbitrator by filing appropriate petitions on 07.02.2023 under Section 3-G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.
It is therefore submitted that there is no merit in the petition and the same is liable to be dismissed.

5. By way of reply, learned Senior counsel for the petitioners submit that since the respondents had themselves challenged the first / original awards before the Deputy Commissioner/ Statutory Arbitrator, the dispute involved in the present petition and the challenge to the impugned revised /
modified awards by the petitioners may also be referred to the very same Deputy Commissioner/
Statutory Arbitrator to be considered and disposed of along with the petitions filed by the respondents.
6.

Upon perusal of the material on record, it is noticed that the subject matter of dispute between the parties is with regard to quantum of compensation payable to the petitioners / land losers and other land losers covered by the very same Notifications.

Under these circumstances, though several contentions have been urged by this Court with regard to the quantum of compensation payable by the respondents in favour of the petitioners in the present writ petition, without expressing any opinion on the merits/ demerits of the rival contentions, I deem it just and proper to dispose of this writ petition referring the dispute involved in the present petition with regard to quantum of compensation payable to the petitioners as well as the legality, validity and correctness of the impugned awards to the Deputy Commissioner/ Statutory Arbitrator before whom, the petitions filed by the respondents challenging the first / original awards passed by the respondents which were subject matter of Valerial Sequeria's case (supra) are pending adjudication for disposal in accordance with law.
7.
